21 @[builtin_term_elab coeNotation] def elabCoe : TermElab := fun stx expectedType? => do
22   let stx := stx[1]
23   tryPostponeIfNoneOrMVar expectedType?
24   let e ← elabTerm stx none
25   if expectedType?.isNone then
26     throwError "invalid coercion notation, expected type is not known"
27   ensureHasType expectedType? e

43 @[builtin_term_elab anonymousCtor] def elabAnonymousCtor : TermElab := fun stx expectedType? =>
44   match stx with
45   | `(⟨$args,*⟩) => do
46     tryPostponeIfNoneOrMVar expectedType?
47     let throwExpTypeUnknown {α} : TermElabM α :=
48       throwError "Invalid `⟨...⟩` notation: The expected type of this term could not be determined"
49     let usageNote := .note m!"\
50       This notation can only be used when the expected type is an inductive type with a single constructor"
51     match expectedType? with
52     | some expectedType =>
53       let expectedType ← whnf expectedType
54       if expectedType.getAppFn.isMVar then throwExpTypeUnknown
55       matchConstInduct expectedType.getAppFn
56         (fun _ => throwError m!"Invalid `⟨...⟩` notation: The expected type{inlineExpr expectedType}is not an inductive type"
57                     ++ usageNote)
58         (fun ival _ => do
59           match ival.ctors with
60           | [ctor] =>
61             if (← isInaccessiblePrivateName ctor) then
62               throwError "Invalid `⟨...⟩` notation: Constructor for `{ival.name}` is marked as private"
63             let cinfo ← getConstInfoCtor ctor
64             let numExplicitFields ← forallTelescopeReducing cinfo.type fun xs _ => do
65               let mut n := 0
66               for h : i in cinfo.numParams...xs.size do
67                 if (← getFVarLocalDecl xs[i]).binderInfo.isExplicit then
68                   n := n + 1
69               return n
70             let mut args := args.getElems
71             if args.size < numExplicitFields then
72               let fieldsStr := if numExplicitFields == 1 then "fields" else "field"
73               let providedStr :=
74                 if args.size == 0 then "none were"
75                 else if args.size == 1 then "only 1 was"
76                 else s!"only {args.size} were"
77               let errMsg := m!"Insufficient number of fields for `⟨...⟩` constructor: Constructor \
78                 `{ctor}` has {numExplicitFields} explicit {fieldsStr}, but {providedStr} provided"
79               if (← read).errToSorry then
80                 logError errMsg
81               else
82                 throwError errMsg
83               for _ in args.size...numExplicitFields do
84                 let s ← mkLabeledSorry (← mkFreshTypeMVar) (synthetic := true) (unique := false)
85                 args := args.push <| ← exprToSyntax s
86             let newStx ← if args.size == numExplicitFields then
87               `($(mkCIdentFrom stx ctor (canonical := true)) $(args)*)
88             else if numExplicitFields == 0 then
89               throwError "Insufficient number of fields for `⟨...⟩` constructor: Constructor \
90                 `{ctor}` does not have explicit fields, but {args.size} \
91                 {if args.size == 1 then "was" else "were"} provided"
92             else
93               let extra := args[(numExplicitFields-1)...args.size]
94               let newLast ← `(⟨$[$extra],*⟩)
95               let newArgs := args[*...(numExplicitFields-1)].toArray.push newLast
96               `($(mkCIdentFrom stx ctor (canonical := true)) $(newArgs)*)
97             withMacroExpansion stx newStx $ elabTerm newStx expectedType?
98           | [] => throwError "Invalid `⟨...⟩` notation: The expected type{inlineExpr expectedType}has no constructors"
99           | _ => throwError m!"Invalid `⟨...⟩` notation: The expected type{inlineExpr expectedType}has more than one constructor"
100                   ++ usageNote)
101     | none => throwExpTypeUnknown
102   | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

109 @[builtin_macro Lean.Parser.Term.show] def expandShow : Macro := fun stx =>
110   match stx with
111   | `(show $type by%$b $tac) => `(show $type from by%$b $tac)
112   | _                        => Macro.throwUnsupported

114 @[builtin_term_elab Lean.Parser.Term.show] def elabShow : TermElab := fun stx expectedType? => do
115   match stx with
116   | `(show $type from $val)  =>
117     /-
118     We first elaborate the type and try to unify it with the expected type if available.
119     Note that, we should not throw an error if the types do not unify. Recall that we have coercions and
120     the following is supported in Lean 3 and 4.
121     ```
122     example : Int :=
123       show Nat from 0
124     ```
125     -/
126     let type ← withSynthesize (postpone := .yes) do
127       let type ← elabType type
128       if let some expectedType := expectedType? then
129         -- Recall that a similar approach is used when elaborating applications
130         discard <| isDefEq expectedType type
131       return type
132     /-
133     Recall that we do not use the same approach used to elaborate type ascriptions.
134     For the `($val : $type)` notation, we just elaborate `val` using `type` and
135     ensure it has type `type`. This approach only ensure the type resulting expression
136     is definitionally equal to `type`. For the `show` notation we use `have` to ensure the type
137     of the resulting expression is *structurally equal* `type`. Structural equality is important,
138     for example, if the resulting expression is a `simp`/`rw` parameter. Here is an example:
139     ```
140     example (x : Nat) : (x + 0) + y = x + y := by
141       rw [show x + 0 = x from rfl]
142     ```
143     -/
144     let thisId := mkIdentFrom stx `this
145     let valNew ← `(have $thisId:ident : $(← exprToSyntax type) := $val; $thisId)
146     elabTerm valNew expectedType?
147   | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
148 
149 @[builtin_macro Lean.Parser.Term.suffices] def expandSuffices : Macro
150   | `(suffices%$tk $x:ident      : $type from $val; $body)   => `(have%$tk $x:ident : $type := $body; $val)
151   | `(suffices%$tk _%$x          : $type from $val; $body)   => `(have%$tk _%$x : $type := $body; $val)
152   | `(suffices%$tk $hy:hygieneInfo $type from $val; $body)   => `(have%$tk $hy:hygieneInfo : $type := $body; $val)
153   | `(suffices%$tk $x:ident      : $type $b:byTactic'; $body) =>
154     -- Pass on `SourceInfo` of `b` to `have`. This is necessary to display the goal state in the
155     -- trailing whitespace of `by` and sound since `byTactic` and `byTactic'` are identical.
156     let b := ⟨b.raw.setKind `Lean.Parser.Term.byTactic⟩
157     `(have%$tk $x:ident : $type := $body; $b:byTactic)
158   | `(suffices%$tk _%$x          : $type $b:byTactic'; $body) =>
159     let b := ⟨b.raw.setKind `Lean.Parser.Term.byTactic⟩
160     `(have%$tk _%$x : $type := $body; $b:byTactic)
161   | `(suffices%$tk $hy:hygieneInfo $type $b:byTactic'; $body) =>
162     let b := ⟨b.raw.setKind `Lean.Parser.Term.byTactic⟩
163     `(have%$tk $hy:hygieneInfo : $type := $body; $b:byTactic)
164   | _ => Macro.throwUnsupported

167 private def elabParserMacroAux (prec e : Term) (withAnonymousAntiquot : Bool) : TermElabM Syntax := do
168   let (some declName) ← getDeclName?
169     | throwError "invalid `leading_parser` macro, it must be used in definitions"
170   match extractMacroScopes declName with
171   | { name := .str _ s, .. } =>
172     let kind := quote declName
173     let mut p ← ``(withAntiquot
174       (mkAntiquot $(quote s) $kind $(quote withAnonymousAntiquot))
175       (leadingNode $kind $prec $e))
176     -- cache only unparameterized parsers
177     if (← getLCtx).all (·.isAuxDecl) then
178       p ← ``(withCache $kind $p)
179     return p
180   | _  => throwError "invalid `leading_parser` macro, unexpected declaration name"
181 
182 @[builtin_term_elab «leading_parser»] def elabLeadingParserMacro : TermElab :=
183   adaptExpander fun
184     | `(leading_parser $[: $prec?]? $[(withAnonymousAntiquot := $anon?)]? $e) =>
185         elabParserMacroAux (prec?.getD (quote Parser.maxPrec)) e (anon?.all (·.raw.isOfKind ``Parser.Term.trueVal))
186     | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

188 private def elabTParserMacroAux (prec lhsPrec e : Term) : TermElabM Syntax := do
189   let declName? ← getDeclName?
190   match declName? with
191   | some declName => let kind := quote declName; ``(Lean.Parser.trailingNode $kind $prec $lhsPrec $e)
192   | none          => throwError "invalid `trailing_parser` macro, it must be used in definitions"
193 
194 @[builtin_term_elab «trailing_parser»] def elabTrailingParserMacro : TermElab :=
195   adaptExpander fun stx => match stx with
196   | `(trailing_parser$[:$prec?]?$[:$lhsPrec?]? $e) =>
197     elabTParserMacroAux (prec?.getD <| quote Parser.maxPrec) (lhsPrec?.getD <| quote 0) e
198   | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

200 @[builtin_term_elab Lean.Parser.Term.panic] def elabPanic : TermElab := fun stx expectedType? => do
201   match stx with
202   | `(panic! $arg) =>
203     let pos ← getRefPosition
204     let env ← getEnv
205     let stxNew ← match (← getDeclName?) with
206     | some declName => `(panicWithPosWithDecl $(quote (toString env.mainModule)) $(quote (toString declName)) $(quote pos.line) $(quote pos.column) $arg)
207     | none => `(panicWithPos $(quote (toString env.mainModule)) $(quote pos.line) $(quote pos.column) $arg)
208     withMacroExpansion stx stxNew $ elabTerm stxNew expectedType?
209   | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

246 /-- Return syntax `Prod.mk elems[0] (Prod.mk elems[1] ... (Prod.mk elems[elems.size - 2] elems[elems.size - 1])))` -/
247 partial def mkPairs (elems : Array Term) : MacroM Term :=
248   let rec loop (i : Nat) (acc : Term) := do
249     if i > 0 then
250       let i    := i - 1
251       let elem := elems[i]!
252       let acc ← `(Prod.mk $elem $acc)
253       loop i acc
254     else
255       pure acc
256   loop (elems.size - 1) elems.back!
257 
258 /-- Return syntax `PProd.mk elems[0] (PProd.mk elems[1] ... (PProd.mk elems[elems.size - 2] elems[elems.size - 1])))` -/
259 partial def mkPPairs (elems : Array Term) : MacroM Term :=
260   let rec loop (i : Nat) (acc : Term) := do
261     if i > 0 then
262       let i    := i - 1
263       let elem := elems[i]!
264       let acc ← `(PProd.mk $elem $acc)
265       loop i acc
266     else
267       pure acc
268   loop (elems.size - 1) elems.back!
269 
270 /-- Return syntax `MProd.mk elems[0] (MProd.mk elems[1] ... (MProd.mk elems[elems.size - 2] elems[elems.size - 1])))` -/
271 partial def mkMPairs (elems : Array Term) : MacroM Term :=
272   let rec loop (i : Nat) (acc : Term) := do
273     if i > 0 then
274       let i    := i - 1
275       let elem := elems[i]!
276       let acc ← `(MProd.mk $elem $acc)
277       loop i acc
278     else
279       pure acc
280   loop (elems.size - 1) elems.back!

283 open Parser

285 def isCDotBinderKind (k : SyntaxNodeKind) : Bool :=
286   k == ``Term.paren || k == ``Term.typeAscription || k == ``Term.tuple
287 
288 /--
289 Returns whether or not this cdot is for the given `HygieneInfo` name;
290 if no hygiene info is given, then matches any cdot, no matter its hygieneInfo.
291 -/
292 def isCDotForInfo (s : Syntax) (hygieneInfo? : Option Name) : Bool :=
293   match s with
294   | `(· $h:hygieneInfo) =>
295     if let some info := hygieneInfo? then
296       h.getHygieneInfo == info
297     else
298       true
299   | _ => false
300 
301 /--
302 Returns true if the given expression contains a cdot for the given `HygieneInfo` name.
303 If no `HygieneInfo` name is given, then returns true if there is any cdot.
304 The search is delimited by cdot binders (any syntax satisfying `isCDotBinderKind`).
305 -/
306 partial def hasCDot : Syntax → Option Name → Bool
307   | s@(Syntax.node _ k args), info? =>
308     if isCDotBinderKind k then false
309     else if isCDotForInfo s info? then true
310     else args.any (fun s => hasCDot s info?)
311   | _, _ => false
312 
313 end
314 
315 /--
316 If the term contains any cdots that match the given `HygieneInfo` name (see `isCDotForInfo`),
317 then returns `some` with the expanded syntax, otherwise returns `none`.
318 
319 Examples:
320 - `· + 1` => `fun x => x + 1`
321 - `f · · b` => `fun x1 x2 => f x1 x2 b`
322 -/
323 partial def expandCDot? (stx : Term) (hygieneInfo? : Option Name) : MacroM (Option Term) := do
324   if hasCDot stx hygieneInfo? then
325     withFreshMacroScope do
326       let mut (newStx, binders) ← (go stx).run #[]
327       if binders.size == 1 then
328         -- It is nicer using `x` over `x1` if there is only a single binder.
329         let x1 := binders[0]!
330         let x ← mkVarFrom x1 "x"
331         binders := binders.set! 0 x
332         newStx ← newStx.replaceM fun s => pure (if s == x1 then x else none)
333       `(fun $binders* => $(⟨newStx⟩))
334   else
335     pure none
336 where
337   mkVarFrom (ref : Syntax) (s : String) : MacroM Ident := do
338     -- We do not incorporate the hygieneInfo macro scopes into the variable name.
339     -- We could, but since cdot function binders identifiers are not supposed to cross stages it would not enable anything.
340     let name ← MonadQuotation.addMacroScope <| Name.mkSimple s
341     return mkIdentFrom ref name (canonical := true)
342   /--
343   Auxiliary function for expanding the `·` notation.
344   The extra state `Array Syntax` contains the new binder names.
345   If `stx` is a `·`, we create a fresh identifier, store it in the
346   extra state, and return it. Otherwise, we just return `stx`.
347   -/
348   go (stx : Syntax) : StateT (Array Ident) MacroM Syntax :=
349     match stx with
350     | .node _ k args => do
351       if isCDotForInfo stx hygieneInfo? then
352         let id ← mkVarFrom stx s!"x{(← get).size + 1}"
353         modify (fun s => s.push id)
354         pure id
355       else if isCDotBinderKind k then
356         pure stx
357       else
358         let args ←
359           if k == choiceKind then
360             if args.isEmpty then
361               return stx
362             let s ← get
363             let args' ← args.mapM (fun arg => go arg |>.run s)
364             let s' := args'[0]!.2
365             unless args'.all (fun (_, s'') => s''.size == s'.size) do
366               Macro.throwErrorAt stx "Ambiguous notation in cdot function has different numbers of '·' arguments in each alternative."
367             set s'
368             pure <| args'.map Prod.fst
369           else
370             args.mapM go
371         return .node (.fromRef stx (canonical := true)) k args
372     | _ => pure stx
373 
374 /--
375   Helper method for elaborating terms such as `(.+.)` where a constant name is expected.
376   This method is usually used to implement tactics that take function names as arguments
377   (e.g., `simp`).
378 -/
379 def elabCDotFunctionAlias? (stx : Term) : TermElabM (Option Expr) := do
380   let some stx ← liftMacroM <| expandCDotArg? stx | pure none
381   let stx ← liftMacroM <| expandMacros stx
382   match stx with
383   | `(fun $binders* => $f $args*) =>
384     if binders.raw.toList.isPerm args.raw.toList then
385       try Term.resolveId? f catch _ => return none
386     else
387       return none
388   | `(fun $binders* => binop% $f $a $b)
389   | `(fun $binders* => binop_lazy% $f $a $b)
390   | `(fun $binders* => leftact% $f $a $b)
391   | `(fun $binders* => rightact% $f $a $b)
392   | `(fun $binders* => binrel% $f $a $b)
393   | `(fun $binders* => binrel_no_prop% $f $a $b) =>
394     if binders == #[a, b] || binders == #[b, a] then
395       try Term.resolveId? f catch _ => return none
396     else
397       return none
398   | `(fun $binders* => unop% $f $a) =>
399     if binders == #[a] then
400       try Term.resolveId? f catch _ => return none
401     else
402       return none
403   | _ => return none
404 where
405   expandCDotArg? (stx : Term) : MacroM (Option Term) :=
406     match stx with
407     | `(($h:hygieneInfo $e)) => Term.expandCDot? e h.getHygieneInfo
408     | _ => Term.expandCDot? stx none
409 
410 @[builtin_macro Lean.Parser.Term.paren] def expandParen : Macro
411   | `(($h:hygieneInfo $e)) => return (← expandCDot? e h.getHygieneInfo).getD e
412   | _       => Macro.throwUnsupported
413 
414 @[builtin_macro Lean.Parser.Term.tuple] def expandTuple : Macro
415   | `(()) => ``(Unit.unit)
416   | `(($h:hygieneInfo $e, $es,*)) => do
417     let pairs ← mkPairs (#[e] ++ es)
418     return (← expandCDot? pairs h.getHygieneInfo).getD pairs
419   | _ => Macro.throwUnsupported
420 
421 @[builtin_macro Lean.Parser.Term.typeAscription] def expandTypeAscription : Macro
422   | `(($h:hygieneInfo $e : $(type)?)) => do
423     match (← expandCDot? e h.getHygieneInfo) with
424     | some e => `(($e : $(type)?))
425     | none   => Macro.throwUnsupported
426   | _ => Macro.throwUnsupported
427 
428 @[builtin_term_elab typeAscription] def elabTypeAscription : TermElab
429   | `(($e : $type)), _ => do
430     let type ← withSynthesize (postpone := .yes) <| elabType type
431     let e ← elabTerm e type
432     ensureHasType type e
433   | `(($e :)), expectedType? => do
434     let e ← withSynthesize (postpone := .no) <| elabTerm e none
435     ensureHasType expectedType? e
436   | _, _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

438 /-- Return `true` if `lhs` is a free variable and `rhs` does not depend on it. -/
439 private def isSubstCandidate (lhs rhs : Expr) : MetaM Bool :=
440   if lhs.isFVar then
441     return !(← dependsOn rhs lhs.fvarId!)
442   else
443     return false
444 
445 /--
446   Given an expression `e` that is the elaboration of `stx`, if `e` is a free variable, then return `k stx`.
447   Otherwise, return `(fun x => k x) e`
448 -/
449 private def withLocalIdentFor (stx : Term) (e : Expr) (k : Term → TermElabM Expr) : TermElabM Expr := do
450   if e.isFVar then
451     k stx
452   else
453     let id ← mkFreshUserName `h
454     let aux ← withLocalDeclD id (← inferType e) fun x => do mkLambdaFVars #[x] (← k (mkIdentFrom stx id))
455     return mkApp aux e
456 
457 @[builtin_term_elab subst] def elabSubst : TermElab := fun stx expectedType? => do
458   let expectedType? ← tryPostponeIfHasMVars? expectedType?
459   match stx with
460   | `($heqStx ▸ $hStx) => do
461      synthesizeSyntheticMVars
462      let mut heq ← withSynthesize <| elabTerm heqStx none
463      let heqType ← inferType heq
464      let heqType ← instantiateMVars heqType
465      match (← Meta.matchEq? heqType) with
466      | none => throwError "invalid `▸` notation, argument{indentExpr heq}\n\
467         has type{indentExpr heqType}\n\
468         equality expected\
469         {← Term.hintAutoImplicitFailure heq (expected := "an equality")}"
470      | some (α, lhs, rhs) =>
471        let mut lhs := lhs
472        let mut rhs := rhs
473        let mkMotive (lhs typeWithLooseBVar : Expr) := do
474          withLocalDeclD (← mkFreshUserName `x) α fun x => do
475            withLocalDeclD (← mkFreshUserName `h) (← mkEq lhs x) fun h => do
476              mkLambdaFVars #[x, h] $ typeWithLooseBVar.instantiate1 x
477        match expectedType? with
478        | some expectedType =>
479          let mut expectedAbst ← kabstract expectedType rhs
480          unless expectedAbst.hasLooseBVars do
481            expectedAbst ← kabstract expectedType lhs
482            unless expectedAbst.hasLooseBVars do
483              throwError "invalid `▸` notation, expected result type of cast is {indentExpr expectedType}\nhowever, the equality {indentExpr heq}\nof type {indentExpr heqType}\ndoes not contain the expected result type on either the left or the right hand side"
484            heq ← mkEqSymm heq
485            (lhs, rhs) := (rhs, lhs)
486          let hExpectedType := expectedAbst.instantiate1 lhs
487          let (h, badMotive?) ← withRef hStx do
488            let h ← elabTerm hStx hExpectedType
489            try
490              return (← ensureHasType hExpectedType h, none)
491            catch ex =>
492              -- if `rhs` occurs in `hType`, we try to apply `heq` to `h` too
493              let hType ← inferType h
494              let hTypeAbst ← kabstract hType rhs
495              unless hTypeAbst.hasLooseBVars do
496                throw ex
497              let hTypeNew := hTypeAbst.instantiate1 lhs
498              unless (← isDefEq hExpectedType hTypeNew) do
499                throw ex
500              let motive ← mkMotive rhs hTypeAbst
501              if !(← isTypeCorrect motive) then
502                return (h, some motive)
503              else
504                return (← mkEqRec motive h (← mkEqSymm heq), none)
505          let motive ← mkMotive lhs expectedAbst
506          if badMotive?.isSome || !(← isTypeCorrect motive) then
507            -- Before failing try to use `subst`
508            if ← (isSubstCandidate lhs rhs <||> isSubstCandidate rhs lhs) then
509              withLocalIdentFor heqStx heq fun heqStx => do
510                let h ← instantiateMVars h
511                if h.hasMVar then
512                  -- If `h` has metavariables, we try to elaborate `hStx` again after we substitute `heqStx`
513                  -- Remark: re-elaborating `hStx` may be problematic if `hStx` contains the `lhs` of `heqStx` which will be eliminated by `subst`
514                  let stxNew ← `(by subst $heqStx; exact $hStx)
515                  withMacroExpansion stx stxNew (elabTerm stxNew expectedType)
516                else
517                  withLocalIdentFor hStx h fun hStx => do
518                    let stxNew ← `(by subst $heqStx; exact $hStx)
519                    withMacroExpansion stx stxNew (elabTerm stxNew expectedType)
520            else
521              throwError "invalid `▸` notation, failed to compute motive for the substitution"
522          else
523            mkEqRec motive h heq
524        | none =>
525          let h ← elabTerm hStx none
526          let hType ← inferType h
527          let mut hTypeAbst ← kabstract hType lhs
528          unless hTypeAbst.hasLooseBVars do
529            hTypeAbst ← kabstract hType rhs
530            unless hTypeAbst.hasLooseBVars do
531              throwError "invalid `▸` notation, the equality{indentExpr heq}\nhas type {indentExpr heqType}\nbut neither side of the equality is mentioned in the type{indentExpr hType}"
532            heq ← mkEqSymm heq
533            (lhs, rhs) := (rhs, lhs)
534          let motive ← mkMotive lhs hTypeAbst
535          unless (← isTypeCorrect motive) do
536            throwError "invalid `▸` notation, failed to compute motive for the substitution"
537          mkEqRec motive h heq
538   | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
539 
540 @[builtin_term_elab stateRefT] def elabStateRefT : TermElab := fun stx _ => do
541   let σ ← elabType stx[1]
542   let mut mStx := stx[2]
543   if mStx.getKind == ``Lean.Parser.Term.macroDollarArg then
544     mStx := mStx[1]
545   let m ← elabTerm mStx (← mkArrow (mkSort levelOne) (mkSort levelOne))
546   let ω ← mkFreshExprMVar (mkSort levelOne)
547   let stWorld ← mkAppM ``STWorld #[ω, m]
548   discard <| mkInstMVar stWorld
549   mkAppM ``StateRefT' #[ω, σ, m]
550 
551 @[builtin_term_elab noindex] def elabNoindex : TermElab := fun stx expectedType? => do
552   let e ← elabTerm stx[1] expectedType?
553   return DiscrTree.mkNoindexAnnotation e
554 
555 @[builtin_term_elab «unsafe»]
556 def elabUnsafe : TermElab := fun stx expectedType? =>
557   match stx with
558   | `(unsafe $t) => do
559     let t ← elabTermAndSynthesize t expectedType?
560     if (← logUnassignedUsingErrorInfos (← getMVars t)) then
561       throwAbortTerm
562     let t ← mkAuxDefinitionFor (← mkAuxName `unsafe) t
563     let .const unsafeFn unsafeLvls .. := t.getAppFn | unreachable!
564     let .defnInfo unsafeDefn ← getConstInfo unsafeFn | unreachable!
565     let implName ← mkAuxName `unsafe_impl
566     addDecl <| Declaration.opaqueDecl {
567       name        := implName
568       type        := unsafeDefn.type
569       levelParams := unsafeDefn.levelParams
570       value       := (← mkOfNonempty unsafeDefn.type)
571       isUnsafe    := false
572     }
573     setImplementedBy implName unsafeFn
574     return mkAppN (Lean.mkConst implName unsafeLvls) t.getAppArgs
575   | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
576 
577 /-- Elaborator for `by_elab`. -/
578 @[builtin_term_elab byElab] def elabRunElab : TermElab := fun stx expectedType? =>
579   match stx with
580   | `(by_elab $cmds:doSeq) => do
581     if let `(Lean.Parser.Term.doSeq| $e:term) := cmds then
582       if e matches `(Lean.Parser.Term.doSeq| fun $[$_args]* => $_) then
583         let tac ← unsafe evalTerm
584           (Option Expr → TermElabM Expr)
585           (Lean.mkForall `x .default
586             (mkApp (Lean.mkConst ``Option) (Lean.mkConst ``Expr))
587             (mkApp (Lean.mkConst ``TermElabM) (Lean.mkConst ``Expr))) e
588         return ← tac expectedType?
589     (← unsafe evalTerm (TermElabM Expr) (mkApp (Lean.mkConst ``TermElabM) (Lean.mkConst ``Expr))
590       (← `(do $cmds)))
591   | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
592 
593 end Lean.Elab.Term
